newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices fall but up from lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices fall but up from lows.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices tumbled as much as 1-1/2 points as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony spurred concerns that he would tighten interest rates.
However, in late trade some of the pressure eased, with prices assessed from down 7/8ths of a point to about 1-1/8th of a point, a municipal analyst said.

The sharp move down forced Florida Municipal Power Agency to scrap a $57.2 million revenue refunding bond, according to its financial advisor, who explained that it would have failed to achieve sufficient savings.
Goldman Sachs & Co had submitted the winning bid for the competitive deal with a true interest cost of 5.4473 percent.
The Municipal Assistance Corp for New York City repriced its $465 million offering by raising yields in most maturities and lifting the top yield in 2008 by five basis points to 5.05 percent.
Still, traders said the new offerings appeared to do fairly well in the teeth of the deteriorating market.
"We saw reasonable, non-panic pricing," the municipal analyst said. Activity in the secondary market was fairly light.

Traders focused on the Federal Reserve chairman's questioning whether equity markets could sustain their big gains, a sentiment he also voiced in December, sending t financial markets reeling when he warned of "irrational exuberance."

And on Wednesday, he also made it plain that while inflation was quiescent, he saw what he called upside risks on the price front and made clear that the central bank was prepared to raise rates if needed to keep inflation down.
"I believe that was a pretty strong indication of what will happen on March 25," said the municipal analyst, referring to the next meeting planned for the Federal Reserve's policy marking body.
March U.S. Treasury bond futures fell 55 ticks to 110-28/32, while the March U.S. municipal bond futures fell 1-10/32 to 115-25/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 157 ticks.
Denver Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of November 2025, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were offered at 5.67 percent, NET, down 10 basis points.
And Jefferson County Alabama Sewer Revenues of February 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.69 percent, NET, down seven basis points.
